100% American-Made Highland 60 Camper Is One of the Most Compact and Rugged – Even Handles Families
17 photos
Photo: Sasquatch Campers
There are so many ways that camper and RV manufacturers position themselves in the industry, and some just take it all the way, about as far as they can. One team that appears to be doing just that is Sasquatch Campers, an American-born name that does it all in the US.
It’s here that we find the Highland 60, a travel trailer that, while it’s built to look and function like a utility trailer, is in fact, a year-round-ready habitat that can have you enjoying the glamping lifestyle in places some campers only dream of; limitless exploration and all you need is to add water.
However, limitless and worry-free glamping is not cheap, and a standard 60, the Pro, is priced starting at $58,500 (€54,000), so clearly, Sasquatch plays the camper game on a different level than most with a similar styling and utility.
Photo: Sasquatch Campers One major reason why we’re asked to drop this much on this camper has to do with the way the body is built. Insulated panels make up the shell, ready with an aluminum exterior and PVC interior walls with wood grain look. Those exterior lockers and roof-rack are also aluminum.
Furthermore, the running gear is in fact built around a tried and tested trailing A-arm setup, one of the most respected and called upon systems for off-roading, and the one under the 60 calls upon integrated Fox shocks. BFGoodrich tires around alloy wheels completes the running gear. Let’s not forget about electric brakes and articulating hitch.
Back to the shell for a minute, I need to point out that this one is strong enough to handle quite the extra goodies and features, and aside from the side-mounted lockers, one of which includes a shower and water heater, the roof and its rack is strong enough to accommodate a roof-top tent. This feature expands sleeping capacity to at least four, depending on the size of your tent.
Photo: Sasquatch Campers If you do call upon this system, do consider that some Highland 60 owners use the storage tray on top of the nose cone utility box for placing a diesel heater or AC unit for the tent, depending on the season.
As a camper that’s designed to drive deep into virgin territory, you need to be prepared for the unexpected, and while there’s already ample space for extras all over the camper, Sasquatch does integrate those Molle panel rails over the cargo boxes.
It’s here that we can bring along shovels, recovery boards, wheel chocks, chains, ropes, you name it and whatever can be exposed to the elements. Do take note of something called the ‘Squatch box, a little storage system underneath the roof rack where we can hide solar panels and an outdoor camping table.
Since I mentioned the utility box, let’s continue to explore this very feature, and as we do, keep in mind the starting price of this camper. First off, we have the bulkhead, ready with AC power socket, shore power input, and solar too.
Photo: Sasquatch Campers But, inside, we find up to 640 Ah lithium with a 1,000 W inverter (standard) and easy to use switch between charging solutions , including combined use from both solar and shore power, at the same time. A Renogy solar charge controller with bluetooth connectivity is also in place and so is a 20 A DC-DC charger with 7-pin connection.
Now, most campers of this style place the kitchen at the rear of the unit, and this is true for the 60 as well. However, there are some unique spins to the space that places the Highland in a class of its own, at least, when compared to teardrop campers.
To access the space, we first swing open the spare tire mount and arm to expose the rear hatch, which also opens to the side, and as it does, it reveals a galley block that is one of the neatest I’ve seen in a while. Aside from the three-burner top and sink with folding faucet that’s integrated into the top, I want to point out the placement of the fridge.
Photo: Sasquatch Campers It’s mounted right onto a tabletop that’s integrated on the interior of the hatch we opened, and according to Sasquatch, this fridge can be removed and the top used as another prep space. Another drop-down table is located on the spare tire arm.
Together, these surfaces grant us access to one of the most expansive kitchens in a camper of this size that I’ve seen in quite some time. Thirty six gallons of freshwater is available for consumption and cleaning.
Inside the unit and unlike just about any utility trailer out there, we do find a space that’s built for sleeping, and can accommodate a queen mattress, has space for personal items, control panels with USBs, and reading lights. Be sure to take note of the double-door design, where one layer is an insect screen. Propane heating is to be used for winter camping, and in summer, a fan and AC.
Photo: Sasquatch Campers Personally, I love what the Highland 60 brings to the table and how it can be so equipped and even easy to use. Check out the little video below to show you a bit about what I mean.
I’m curious to hear your thoughts on this glamping solution; there’s a comment section below.

Air cargo carries the world’s most time-critical goods, yet for decades it ran on paper, phone calls and spreadsheets. That is changing, and the industry now has the data foundation to do more with it.
The new foundation is AI. Not AI for its own sake, but AI pointed at the three outcomes that decide whether a cargo business wins: lower cost, higher revenue and less risk.
Building the digital foundation
Air cargo is a complex, multi-party business. Every shipment touches an airline, a forwarder, a ground handler, customs and often a last-mile carrier, each with its own systems. Connecting them all takes time, and the industry has been making steady progress.
IATA has made it a priority. At the 2026 World Cargo Symposium it noted that fragmented data systems still create inefficiencies, especially in high-volume segments like e-commerce.
That foundation is now well underway. The electronic air waybill has been an IATA standard since 2010 and sits near 80% adoption on enabled lanes. In January 2026, ONE Record became IATA’s preferred standard for end-to-end cargo data exchange, and airlines carrying more than 70% of global air waybill volume are on track to implement it.
With connected data in place, the next opportunity is putting it to work. Digitizing a waybill saves paper; deciding what to do with the data is what creates value.
The business case: cost, revenue and risk
Air cargo is a hard forecasting problem. Bookings come late, demand swings with the economy, and capacity on a passenger flight shifts with every bag and every gallon of fuel. Two weeks before departure, less than 40% of an airline’s capacity is typically booked, and more than half often fills in the final week. Spreadsheets and rules of thumb cannot keep up with that. Models can.
Cost savings. Across supply chains, McKinsey reports that AI-enabled management can cut logistics costs by up to 15% , lower inventory by 35% and lift service levels by 65%. In cargo terms, that means fewer manual touches, fewer re-keyed messages and less space flown empty.
Revenue optimization. In one McKinsey case , an AI tool cut a cargo airline’s demand-forecast error from about 20% to 14%. Predicting cancellations let another airline overbook with confidence, and together with other use cases it lifted load factors by around 8% after a 12-week pilot. McKinsey also estimates that raising below-average yields in the last week before departure by 30% can grow overall revenue by 7% to 8%.
Risk reduction. Yield volatility peaks in the final days before a flight, exactly when people have the least time to decide. Compliance is getting harder too: IATA counts more than 1,200 state and operator variations on dangerous goods handling.
Start with the business question, not the model
None of this happens by bolting AI onto an old process. McKinsey’s global survey found that only 37% of respondents attribute any EBIT impact to AI, and true high performers are roughly 6% of organizations. Adopting AI is easy; turning it into money is not.
That is why SmartKargo starts every AI capability with one test. Does it reduce risk, drive revenue or reduce cost for the airline? If it does not clearly deliver at least one, it does not ship.
Three principles keep it responsible:
People stay in control. AI recommends; qualified operators decide on pricing, capacity and exceptions, and can override any recommendation.
Recommendations are explainable. Each one shows the data behind it, the factors that weighed most and the model’s confidence.
Airline data stays protected. Encryption, role-based access and continuous monitoring, and data is never shared with other carriers.
Where AI earns its place in cargo
Air cargo generated $149 billion in revenue in 2024 , yet many critical decisions still rely on static rules, manual overrides and delayed reports. Four areas stand out where AI turns existing data into better decisions:
Revenue and capacity ( AIRCAM ). Forecast demand, predict sellable belly space and guide pricing, so more of every flight sells at the right yield.
Operations control ( AINOC ). Predict delays, flag shipments at risk of missing their SLA and rank exceptions, giving teams one clear view of what needs attention first.
ULDs and ground assets ( AIULD ). Track containers and equipment to raise utilization, reduce losses and know where every asset is.
Messaging and interoperability ( AICTX ). Translate and route messages across Cargo-IMP, Cargo-XML, ONE Record and customs systems, so data moves cleanly between partners.
Each use case works best when it plugs into the cargo systems an airline already runs, and when every decision stays with a person.
The bottom line
Air cargo spent years digitizing its paperwork. The next step is putting that data to work on the decisions that set margins: what to sell, at what price, on which flight. Airlines that treat AI as a disciplined business tool, measured against cost, revenue and risk, will pull ahead.
About SmartKargo
SmartKargo is the AI-powered, cloud-based platform that turns airlines into world-class cargo carriers, with cargo management, e-commerce, and AI in one system. Our cargo ERP runs the entire shipment lifecycle, from booking and acceptance to handling, tracking, and last-mile delivery. Our e-commerce solutions let airlines launch parcel products in weeks and connect directly to online retailers. Our AI applications forecast capacity and demand, guide pricing, and optimize load plans, so airlines capture revenue that legacy systems leave on the table. Trusted by airlines across North America, Latin America, India, and beyond, SmartKargo is making every flight a cargo opportunity. SmartKargo is headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, with key offices in India, the Philippines, Brazil, the United Arab Emirates, the United Kingdom, and Canada.

This Custom Australian Tiny Home Is a One-of-a-Kind Retreat With Treehouse Nook and Gorgeous Kitchen
26 photos
Photo: Unplgd Tiny Homes
Australian tiny home builders certainly know how to make the most of a small space while infusing it with character and beauty along the way. Tiny houses from this country often come with really efficient layouts, gorgeous nature-inspired aesthetics, and are built to handle real Australian conditions.
They are also designed specifically for the local landscape, reflecting the surroundings they are placed in and establishing a natural connection with the outdoors. All this is true for this custom tiny house set among gum trees in the Blue Mountains region of New South Wales.
With a single-level layout, unique features such as a treehouse nook and a large entertainer’s kitchne, as well as impressive handcrafted details, this tiny house is a great example of what a smart design, craftsmanship, and creativity can achieve, especially when a home is built to the specific needs of its owner.
This one-of-a-kind model is the creation of Unplgd Tiny Homes, a small, family-run business from New South Wales, and proves that going tiny can feel liberating for many people, as it gives them greater freedom and the possibility to reconnect with nature and what matters to them.
Founded by a couple who wanted to help others find their own version of that freedom, Unplgd Tiny Homes focuses on creating affordable, high-quality compact dwellings full of personality. Not cookie cutter, not one size fits all.
Photo: Unplgd Tiny Homes This particular unit, which was designed for an empty nester who lives alone on a stunning farm property, is described as one of the builder’s most accomplished custom designs to date. It is inspired by the company’s Magpie design but is specifically tailored around the owner’s priorities, her routines, and the way she wanted the home to feel.
This is a tiny home where personalization truly shines and nothing is random. And it is not about just adding extra features for more convenience, but rather about choosing materials and finishes that suit the person living there. As such, the home stands out with gorgeous live-edge timber worktops that feel like a piece of the landscape brought inside, warm cork flooring, timber-framed windows and doors, and fluted cabinets that impress with their warmth and texture.
The color scheme was also carefully considered, combining nature-inspired shades of brown, green, and cream for a calm, welcoming ambiance inside.
Based on a dual-axle trailer, this tiny house measures 11 meters (36 feet) long and 3 meters (10 feet) wide. Its exterior is finished in corrugated metal combined with a durable steel roof. A double glass door and a cross gable section above the entryway give the home a contemporary look.
Photo: Unplgd Tiny Homes The interior boasts spacious and luminous living areas, including a large central kitchen, a downstairs bedroom, a lounge, and a walk-through bathroom. One of the highlights of this custom home is a little treehouse-inspired nook, which was a special request from the owner.
Strategically located at one end of the house, it is basically a raised platform separated from the actual living area by vertical wooden slats. It’s big enough to put a mattress over there and transform it into a cozy place for reading, meditating, watching a movie, or simply relaxing. A big house-shaped window connects this tucked-away corner to the outdoors, making the surrounding scenery part of the living space.
Open cubbies beneath the bed provide accessible storage. They are built with steel beams inside, making them sturdy enough to double as steps leading up to the raised nook. What’s more, two hidden storage compartments are integrated underneath, perfect for storing blankets, pillows, and other items.
Next to the treehouse nook is the living area. It’s quite compact but can comfortably fit a regular sofa positioned opposite the glass entry doors. This arrangement allows the owner to sit back and relax while enjoying both the outside views and the warmth of the fireplace. Tucked neatly next to the glass door is a Charmwood Air3 wood-burning stove surrounded by an area protected with fiber-cement sheeting and fireproof paint.
Photo: Unplgd Tiny Homes Another standout feature is the extra large kitchen with rustic looks and modern functionality . It spans both sides of the house with a spacious U-shaped design on one side and a separate cooking section, floor-to-ceiling cabinets, and a dedicated space for a large fridge on the other. It’s described as an entertainer's kitchen and is really cleverly done.
The client wanted a fully functioning kitchen as she enjoys cooking and baking, so the appliance package was chosen accordingly. She had the space equipped with a large granit sink, a Kleenmaid four-burner induction cooktop, and a multifunctional combi oven.
What immediately catches the eye in this generous kitchen is the beautiful live-edge timber slabs used for the countertops, which bring warmth and character to the space. Underneath the counters, there are plenty of dark blue cabinets, and overhead, even more cupboards with natural wood doors ensure there is plenty of space for all the essentials. A beautiful sandy creamy subway tile backsplash ties everything together.
Photo: Unplgd Tiny Homes The kitchen peninsula nearest to the living room also doubles as a breakfast bar, perfect for dining or occasional snacking. There is also a sliding window above the sink, which can work as a servery window as well. The owner plans to install a fold-out bench outside, allowing this opening to create an easy connection between the indoor kitchen and outdoor entertaining area.
Champagne cork flooring runs throughout these social areas of the house, adding both warmth underfoot and sound insulation. All the windows and doors are framed with spotted gum timber, an Australian hardwood that is durable and naturally resistant to weathering and insects, and the high, vaulted ceilings make the interior feel open and spacious.
Photo: Unplgd Tiny Homes Venturing further into the tiny home , we discover the walk-through bathroom that takes advantage of the home’s full-width to give you enough space to get ready. It features micro-cemented walls, pebble flooring, live-edge timber slabs for the vanity worktop and a shelving system. It also has a custom vanity area with a gorgeous stone sink carved from real stone and a large walk-in shower. The shower feels truly luxurious through its sheer size, the brushed copper rainfall showerhead, a curved separation wall and rounded corners that soften the design.
Stepping into the rear bedroom, we discover a quieter, more intimate atmosphere. The walls are finished in a warm olive green shade, and windows on either side of the bed bring in natural light and a nice breeze. Another show-stopping feature is a cute circular window above the space where the bed goes. This traditional-style bedroom also fits a chest of drawers and a wardrobe, both finished with beautiful green fluted faces, making it feel truly one of a kind.
Due to its easy-to-navigate layout, modern amenities, and gorgeous finishes, this custom tiny home feels comfortable, personal, and practical for everyday life.

By: Northern Miner Staff November 23, 2026
Canadian Copper (CSE: CCI) has reported broad copper-bearing drill intervals west of its Murray Brook deposit in New Brunswick, highlighting potential expansion opportunities as it advances plans to process the ore at the nearby Caribou mill.
Hole MB26-06 cut 54.55 metres grading 0.80% copper from 29.45 metres downhole, including 33.15 metres at 1.14% copper, Canadian Copper said Monday in a statement . Hole MB26-16 returned 40.15 metres at 0.86% copper from 79 metres downhole.
Canadian Copper tested ground up to 50 metres west of the deposit boundary, about 60 km west of Bathurst.
“The combination of broad mineralized intervals, good copper grades, and proximity to our planned mining operations creates an opportunity to potentially improve the project’s economics,” CEO Simon Quick said.
Shares of Canadian Copper rose 13% to 44¢ in Monday afternoon on the Canadian Securities Exchange, valuing the company at about $102 million (US$71 million). They’ve ranged between 32¢ and 82¢ in the past year.
January study
Canadian Copper expects to release a feasibility study in late January on mining Murray Brook and trucking ore 13 km to Caribou. It rushed selected mineralized intervals to the lab and expects complete hole assays in February, subject to lab availability.
The reported intervals are downhole lengths; true widths remain unknown. Further modelling and technical evaluation are needed before the new mineralization can enter a resource estimate or mine plan.
Canadian Copper completed the Caribou acquisition on July 28. The purchase gives it an existing mill, tailings facilities and supporting infrastructure to combine with its wholly owned Murray Brook deposit.
13-year life
A May 2025 preliminary economic assessment outlined an open pit feeding Caribou at 3,300 tonnes a day over more than 13 years. It estimated initial capital costs of $64 million and an after-tax net present value of $171 million at a 7% discount rate, using a copper price of US$4.25 per pound.
The feasibility study was initially scheduled for December, according to a statement released in May when Canadian Copper appointed its study team. Its Nov. 16 update moved the expected release to late January, subject to final engineering and cost estimates. The company also expects an environmental-assessment update in the first quarter of 2027.
In earlier development plans, management envisaged starting work at Murray Brook in 2027 and processing ore in 2028. Those targets depended on environmental review, permits, financing and a development decision.
Canadian Copper reported more than $24 million in treasury on Nov. 16 after receiving about $9.8 million from warrant exercises. It’s also pursuing project funding through streaming and debt arrangements and has continued discussions with Ottawa about potential critical-minerals support.

Is This the Perfect 1970 Charger Project? Still Unrestored, All-Original, 1 of 436
26 photos
Photo: eBay seller mauscha30
Get ready to be impressed. This 1970 Dodge Charger is an ambitious restoration project that landed online specifically with this simple goal in mind. It must find the right person to bring it back to the road, and it hopes that an unrestored configuration with the all-original setup and a matching-numbers powertrain would do it.
That’s right, this Charger checks all the right boxes for a restoration candidate, and that’s why I believe that it won’t be hard for this car to find a new home.
The owner says this Charger has been with the same owner since 1981, and amazingly, it still runs well, as the seller notes. This is even more impressive when considering the unrestored condition, which should technically mean that not even the engine has been touched.
Photo: eBay seller mauscha30 With the Challenger now the model on everybody’s lips, the Charger received less attention. 49,800 units rolled off the assembly lines, and probably the best thing - especially for those who are diehard fans - is that the six-cylinder engine, which didn’t even make much sense on the Charger in the first place - was a lot less popular.
Only 300 people got a six, whereas everybody else went for a V8-powered Charger.
The base engine was the 225ci with 145 horsepower, while the standard V8 configuration was a 318 with 230 horsepower. The 383s ended up becoming the most common equipment on a 1970 Charger, as they developed 290 horsepower and 350 horsepower in the four-barrel configuration.
On the other hand, the Charger continued to be all about powerful engines, so people who didn’t want to stick with the base configuration could go for the big-block options. The R/T was still available with a 440 rated at 375 horsepower, but the almighty engine remained the 426 Street Hemi. It produced 425 horsepower and was a ridiculously expensive upgrade.
Only 112 Chargers produced for this model year got a Hemi.
Photo: eBay seller mauscha30 This Dodge isn’t a Hemi-powered specimen, but what sets it apart from the rest of the crowd is the color it wears. This is Sublime Green, code FJ5, which, according to the seller, made its way to only 436 Chargers produced for this model year.
The paint you see in the photos is still the original spray that was applied to the Charger before it left the factory. Sure, it has clearly seen better days, with quarter panels requiring some attention. I would also raise this Charger on a lift to check the underside because I expect at least some surface rust on the floors, but the seller claims the car has always been garaged, and there’s still hope that the undercarriage damage isn’t significant.
This Charger has always been “meticulously watched after,” according to the seller, but for additional information, especially regarding the previous ownership, you’ll have to reach out to them with all the questions you have in mind.
For example, while we do know that this Charger has been with the same owner since 1981, it’s unclear how many people owned it before this year.
Photo: eBay seller mauscha30 As for the engine that’s now in charge of putting the wheels in motion, the car is fitted with a 383 Magnum V8 engine with a four-barrel carburetor, a manual transmission, and a Pistol-Grip shifter.
This is quite an alright setup, especially because the car has the more powerful version of the 383. It runs and drives well, but it needs some attention, according to the owner, so what I would do is ask my mechanic to go see the car in person and then tell me if the drivetrain will cost high dollars to rebuild.
Without a doubt, the only option for this Charger is a complete restoration, as turning it into a daily driver without spending big on the restoration would be a wasted opportunity to create something truly special. You don’t come across an unrestored and original 1970 Charger with these low production numbers, so I expect that the next time we see this car, it’ll be in a couple of years in tip-top condition.
Photo: eBay seller mauscha30 Meanwhile, the first thing it must do is to convince someone to pay high dollars to take it home. Unsurprisingly, this Charger isn’t affordable, and the owner believes $60,000 is a fair price in its current condition.
The Make Offer option is also enabled, meaning that you might be able to save a few bucks if you have the right negotiation skills and you’re committed to a purchase, but I don’t expect the price to drop significantly.
You can find this Charger in Gouldsboro, Maine, and considering its shape, you should be able to drive it home on its wheels to a nearby location. Anything farther would require transportation, so it’s probably safer to go there in person, check the car live, and then bring your trailer to take it home safely.

Cobalt in the DRC is often found alongside copper and malachite. (Image by Fairphone, Flickr ).
Posted By: Henry Lazenby November 23, 2026
The Democratic Republic of Congo will suspend all cobalt exports from Nov. 30 as prices slide despite restrictions on shipments from the world’s top producer of the battery metal, Reuters and Bloomberg reported Monday, citing the country’s strategic minerals regulator.
The ban covers cobalt from industrial and artisanal mines and has no fixed end date. The regulator, known by its French acronym Arecoms, plans to review the measure after four months and use the suspension to revise how it allocates export quotas. It cited rising inventories and weaker consumption.
Congo supplied about three-quarters of the world’s mined cobalt before it first halted shipments in February 2025. Prices initially rose, but cobalt hydroxide, the main product Congo ships, lost nearly half its value from an April peak, according to Fastmarkets. The Cobalt Institute’s latest quarterly report put the cobalt hydroxide price in Asia at $14.50 (C$20.85) per lb. of contained cobalt on Oct. 14, down 43% since July 1, citing Benchmark Mineral Intelligence data.
The quotas already left a wide gap between what miners produced and what they could sell. China’s CMOC Group produced 99,694 tonnes of cobalt in the first nine months of 2026 and sold just 12,661 tonnes, leaving a difference of 87,033 tonnes between production and sales in that period. Output rose 13% from a year earlier while sales fell 75%.
Sales impact
Glencore (LSE: GLEN) took a different approach. Its cobalt output fell more than half to 13,700 tonnes over the same period. As it focused on copper, Glencore left more of the cobalt it recovered from mixed ore in solution, deferring processing into saleable hydroxide, the company said in its quarterly production report.
Kinshasa replaced its first export ban with quotas in October 2025, setting an export ceiling of 96,600 tonnes for 2026. Of that, 87,000 tonnes were available to producers and 9,600 tonnes were set aside for projects the regulator deemed strategically important.

Honda Details 2028 CR-V's 2.0L Hybrid Powertrain With Available DualPower eAWD
13 photos
Photo: Honda
Honda's next-generation hybrid includes a 2.0-liter naturally aspirated inline-four mill that promises to be more efficient than the CR-V Hybrid's outgoing engine. To be deployed in a multitude of models, including the 2028 model year CR-V, the redesigned hybrid system includes an engine that burns fuel more efficiently, maintaining stoichiometric combustion across a much wider operating range.
Officially branded Honda Hybrid, which is as clinical as it gets in this industry, the new setup further includes a familiar two-motor drive unit, improved thermal management, and an optional electric rear axle. Honda detailed this hybrid system after introducing the second-generation Avancier , namely a sport utility vehicle with three-row seating that Honda assembles in Thailand rather than Japan.
As far as the combustion engine is concerned, stoichiometric combustion is the name of the game. The ideal air-to-fuel ratio sees all oxygen and gasoline reacting completely without excess oxygen or unburned fuel. That's just around 14.7:1 by mass for gasoline, a ratio that allows the cats to clean exhaust gases effectively.
Current-gen engines allow extra fuel under high output to either cool parts or boost power. Honda prefers to speed up combustion rather than relying on richer mixtures to manage either problem. How did the Japanese automaker do it? For starters, the intake port was redesigned, narrowing the relatively straight shape while adding a ski jump-like ramp at its base.
This increases airflow velocity while generating a stronger vertical tumble flow inside the cylinders. The rolling motion of the incoming air-fuel charge is preserved as the piston approaches top dead center, thus creating the turbulence needed to accelerate flame propagation after the spark ignites the mixture. The piston crown has also been revised to retain more of that tumble movement.
Photo: Honda Honda also developed a two-piece water jacket designed to cool both sides of the exhaust port, helping control thermal loading around the combustion chamber. This water jacket further complements the faster burn achieved through the redesigned intake and piston crowns.
Optimized for hybrid applications rather than gasoline-only and hybrid applications, the new engine features a lighter block. The aluminum-alloy block weighs approximately 900 grams (2 pounds) less, while the crankshaft is 500 grams (1 pound) lighter. Revised pin-boss areas, piston skirts, and other components contribute further reductions.
Similar to the outgoing hybrids, the front drive unit retains the parallel-axis arrangement for its generator and traction motors. The new unit is lighter and reduces friction through improved lubrication, bearings, and oil temperature management. Even the magnetic circuits in both motors have been revised, with the generator priding itself on more torque density while using fewer magnets.
Its traction motor uses magnets devoid of heavy rare-earth elements, while thinner electromagnetic steel sheets reduce electrical losses. The power control unit is shorter front to rear by 51 millimeters (2 inches) and 3 percent lighter to boot. Said control unit integrates additional control hardware for the electric AWD system, including the rear drive motor's control chip.
DualPower eAWD implies a 50-kW rear drive unit, with 50 kilowatts converting to either 68 metric horsepower or 67 mechanical ones. During high-speed cruising, an engine direct-drive gear allows the combustion engine to drive the front wheels mechanically.
A water-cooled oil cooler transfers heat between the engine's coolant circuit and the drive unit's lubricating oil. The revised system integrates the cooling circuits for both the front drive unit and the power control unit, which are separate on the 2027 model year CR-V Hybrid.

Xpeng Is Offering Self-Driving Rides in Paris, Might Get EU-Wide Certification Ahead of Tesla
6 photos
Photo: Xpeng
Chinese carmaker Xpeng has started offering self-driving rides in Paris using its Tesla FSD rival Navigation Guided Pilot (NGP). The demo rides are available to visitors to Xpeng's showroom through November 28. This marks not only the first time Xpeng has offered NGP rides outside China, but also the first Chinese carmaker demonstrating its self-driving technology in Europe.
Tesla has long bragged about having the most advanced autonomous driving system in the world. Tesla Full Self-Driving has been praised as having "human-like" behavior and even "superhuman" abilities to sense danger and take evasive maneuvers. Based on FSD, Tesla has also started Cybercab driverless operations in Texas.
However, Elon Musk's company has faced difficulties getting FSD approved in Europe, despite some successes in the Netherlands and a few other markets. The main cause has been Tesla's stubbornness in disregarding UNECE R171 S02 regulations pertaining to advanced driver assistance systems. Instead, Tesla thinks the EU should accept FSD as it was designed in the US by granting it exceptions to the European rules.
That explains why Tesla is still struggling to get approval across the block. Mercedes-Benz, on the other hand, has designed its MB.DRIVE Assist Pro system around those pesky regulations. This allowed it to get the first certification in Germany last week. Another carmaker that also observed UNECE restrictions is Xpeng, which appears to be next in line to steal Tesla's limelight.
Xpeng recently announced its European ambitions and has already started self-driving rides in Paris using its Navigation Guided Pilot (NGP). This is an advanced driver assistance system rivaling both Tesla Assisted Driving (FSD's new name in Europe) and Mercedes-Benz's MB.DRIVE Assist Pro. Xpeng is offering visitors to its Paris showroom self-driving demo rides lasting 30 minutes through November 28.
Xpeng touts being the first Chinese brand to demonstrate its self-driving technology in Europe. It's also the first time Xpeng has showcased its tech outside China. The demo car is a production Xpeng L03 Performance Ultra whose brains are powered by two Turing AI chips. Each of them is rated at 750 trillion operations per second (TOPS).
Xpeng's NGP driverless system is a vision-based system for the most part. However, unlike Tesla's, it also uses radar and ultrasonic sensors for additional input. Despite that, it doesn't appear to be as capable as Tesla Assisted Driving. While the system handled Paris traffic with ease during a demo ride, journalists from the French outlet Caradisiac noticed the car did not stop at an amber traffic light and, a few meters later, it also failed to yield for a pedestrian.
Tesla Assisted Driving is not perfect either, which is why both systems are certified as Level 2 driver assistance systems. This means that they must be supervised at all times, and the driver must be ready to take control at any time. Xpeng plans to offer NGP to European customers in 2027, pending regulatory approval.

NVIDIA GTC 2023 Grace Superchip With Jensen
What an odd few weeks. The big news today, of course, is that Jensen Huang has been reinstated as NVIDIA’s CEO . The markets immediately responded by adding roughly 30% or about $1T in market cap. I think folks realized this was the right option.
Jensen is BACK at NVIDIA
One of the big catalysts to this was that the U.S. government came out and said that they do not believe that having Jensen as the CEO of NVIDIA is a national security risk.
“ In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk. ” ( Source : NVIDIA)
It seems the government sign-off gave the board air cover on one major risk factor: that the Megaspeed issue would turn into a major national security investigation. With that off the table, then there was the challenge of alleged workplace conduct.
NVIDIA GTC 2024 Jensen Approved Samsung HMB3E 12H
Workplace conduct is always a challenge because it opens NVIDIA up to claims from current and former employees. There was an early 2010’s case in California (note I have a 2007 JD from California’s largest law school, but never practiced, so this is not legal advice) for workplace sexual harassment in the $168M range, that was then significantly reduced to under $100M, then settled. What I have been telling folks for the past week and a half is that for the company to lose $1T in shareholder value, even $1B in a legal fund pays a lot of attorneys to cover other claims. It felt like Jensen’s value was wildly out of line with what it would cost to settle the cases. Again, I am not condoning the allegations, but at some point, I would have a hard time believing NVIDIA’s board did not have a team developing a range of exposure if they were to settle claims that could then be weighed against the cost of not having Jensen on the team. When it was comparing those two numbers plus potential government action, I can see how a board would have been more conservative.
Perhaps the other big one is that NVIDIA’s team accepted the news publicly, but what is hard to quantify is that folks who have been at NVIDIA for many years and built this enormous business are very loyal to Jensen. It has been really strange reading mainstream media reports about how Jensen can get passionate in meetings as if that were a major issue. Every CEO, especially founders, gets passionate because the business is personal. I would venture to guess that any of Jensen’s direct reports who have been there for a few years have earned enough to walk away if they wanted to, and they truly did not like working for Jensen. Maybe to put it another way, in the week and a half since Jensen resigned, I never heard an NVIDIA employee say “good riddance” or anything like that. Folks supported the board, but only spoke positively about Jensen’s leadership. It turns out when you create a market segment big enough to be measured in percentage of US GDP, it creates wealth for your employees, suppliers, customers, and partners that makes them loyal. Installing someone from the outside as CEO just does not replace that.
Final Words
More than a few executives were probably hoping to land the role and are disappointed, but realistically, those are hard shoes to fill. Jensen’s focus on the AI supply chain, sales to big customers, and loyalty among employees who have done well under his watch are exceptionally hard for anyone to replicate. Moreover, executives might be able to rise to the job, but NVIDIA added over $55B in revenue last quarter versus the year-ago quarter. Revenue-wise, that is roughly in the ballpark of adding an American Airlines annual revenue to NVIDIA on a quarterly basis. Moving that fast, it is hard for someone to grow in place in that role.
Dell DTW 2026 Keynote Day 1 Jensen
Perhaps the most fascinating part is what this means for executive compensation. The market saw what it meant to have Jensen out as NVIDIA’s CEO not just for NVIDIA, but for others in the ecosystem. Delaware’s compensation cases with Elon Musk now have a new data point showing this class of CEO can have an outsized impact on shareholder value. Not all CEOs are the same, and an individual can be uniquely valuable to an organization. Is Lisa Su the same at AMD? What about Mark Zuckerberg at Meta? Hock Tan at Broadcom? Michael Dell and Jeff Clarke? Or someone like Matt Murphy, who took Marvell from a very rough company a decade ago to a company zipping along today? The other side of this is figuring out the set of circumstances and formula for when a high-flying CEO can be ousted.
Marvell Computex 2026 Keynote Jensen
Personally, I think the board made the right decision in bringing Jensen back to NVIDIA, even if it means some clean-up needs to happen.

Subaru vehicles are known for their dual-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) capabilities, but to cut costs, the company is now offering front-wheel-drive (FWD) versions on select electric models.
Subaru adds FWD, starting with electric vehicles
The Uncharted EV went on sale earlier this year as a smaller, sportier entry-level electric crossover positioned below the Solterra.
It was also the first Subaru model in about 30 years not to come with standard all-wheel drive. After unveiling the Uncharted EV last summer, Subaru said, “For buyers focused on affordability and range, the entry-level Uncharted Premium FWD model will be offered in limited numbers.”
Apparently, it wasn’t too limited. The 2027 Uncharted EV is now on sale, still with the base Premium FWD model equipped with a single 221-horsepower front-mounted electric motor.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Higher-priced Uncharted trims, including the Sport and GT, are upgraded with Subaru’s Symmetrical All-Wheel Drive system with X-Mode, delivering a combined 338 horsepower.
The 2027 Subaru Uncharted EV Premium FWD starts at $34,995, while the Sport and GT are priced from $39,795 and $43,795, respectively.
2027 Subaru Uncharted EV (Source: Subaru)
In the US, the 2027 Solterra and larger Trailseeker are still equipped with standard AWD, but Subaru is introducing new FWD (4×2) variants in some markets at a lower price point.
In comparison, the 2027 Subaru Solterra and Trailseeker EV start at $38,495 and $39,995, respectively.
Subaru opened preorders for its new 2027 electric range in Spain, including the Unchartered, Solterra, and E-Outback, which is sold as the Trailseeker in the US.
2027 Subaru Trailseeker (E-Outback in Europe) (Source: Subaru)
All of which will be available with a lower-priced FWD variant. Like the Uncharted, Subaru will still offer AWD on higher-priced Solterra and E-Outback trims.
The new Subaru Uncharted (4×2) starts at €26,525 ($28,900), the Solterra (4×2) starts at €35,025 ($38,200), and the E-Outback (4×2) starts at €36,525 ($39,800) in Spain , including subsidies, discounts, and other incentives.
2027 Subaru Solterra EV (Source: Subaru)
Preorders are open for the Uncharted, while the Solterra and E-Outback are expected to launch in mid-2027.
Electrek’s Take
Will Subaru expand FWD (4×2) to other vehicles and markets, like the US? The Uncharted is still Subaru’s only EV sold with standard FWD. The 2027 Solterra and Trailseeker are equipped with AWD and X-Mode.
Subaru is already selling considerably more EVs in the US, with three affordable, practical electric SUVs: the Uncharted, Solterra, and Trailseeker.
In Spring 2027, it will add its first three-row electric SUV, the Getaway. It wouldn’t be a surprise to see Subaru introduce a FWD option for other models, like the Solterra, at a lower price point.
Then again, AWD is used significantly more in the US than in Spain and other markets. For now, the Uncharted remains Subaru’s sole FWD model.

Polygon's Latest Tambora Gravel Bike Stands As Their Lightest and Fastest – Priced As Low as $1,800
11 photos
Photo: Polygon Bikes
Bicycles have always been one of the go-to solutions for moving around our cities and over the years, they’ve changed drastically. Even now, trends are taking the cycling world by storm, and we’re about to witness how.
For years, the trusted hardtail MTB was the average Joe’s go-to bicycle, being seem ridden around town, on dirt roads, and even through mountain trails. I remember riding my own to school, to grab groceries, and on the weekends, even hit up some desert trails in Phoenix. However, the past few years have seen the introduction of a different kind of all-rounder bicycle: the gravel bike.
Instead of building the do-it-all spirit around a frame that is technically born to handle woodlands, the gravel frame started off with what is essentially a road-bike, one with a traditional diamond frame, stiff front fork, and even drop bars. Often, gravel tires are narrower than what we see on an MTB, but recent trends are changing all that.
Photo: Polygon Bikes Considering most of us do their riding on tarmac, it just made sense to build a bike upon a design and style that is at home in that very setting. Some differences between a road and gravel bike are also very clear, with one in particular acting as a way to soften up the rear: dropping the seat stays. This allows the seat post to move a bit more freely while also minimizing the size of the rear triangle; the latter also adds more compliance.
Another trait gravel bikes are known for is the presence of drop bars, and since these bikes are often ridden in settings that offer more vibrations and instability than tarmac, handlebar flare is integrated to widen our grip and provide stability. Flares can also cause the body to sit a tad more upright than on a road bike, not to mention the use of risers and different stems.
As the years have gone by, and the gravel bike exposed to more and more R&D, it too has begun to change, with some brands even going as far as integrating fork travel into the design, and even flat bars or straight handlebars, as we often see on MTBs . Teams like SRAM even have dedicated suspension forks for gravel, not to mention entire drivetrain ranges.
Photo: Polygon Bikes All that brings us to the ravishing beast before us today: Polygon Bikes’ latest spin on the gravel ecosystem. What this crew has done here is set their sights on a much more modern and sportier gravel bike, one that even taps into aero tricks and traits we often see on road bikes in order to help riders shave seconds off the clocks. Sources mention that this ones is to now stand as Tambora’s gravel racing flagship.
Furthermore, four separate builds also position the frame to land in the hands of as many people as possible, with prices ranging from under $2,000, $1,800, to be precise, to $4,500, so a bit of everything for everyone, and yes, all use the latest and “lightest gravel platform” this team has ever brought to the market.
While weights for the complete bikes are not mentioned on the manufacturer’s website, sources state that the new frame does weighs just 1,200 grams and can handle a total load of 125 kg (276 lbs).
Photo: Polygon Bikes It’s called ACX, and this carbon fiber frame has been specifically designed to push as much power into that rear wheel as possible while also keeping rider fatigue to a minimum. The geo has been updated to place us in a much more aggressive and aerodynamic position and the wheelbase lengthened for stability.
In terms of compatibility, the new platform can be equipped with 1x or 2x drivetrains, and handles wheels as large as 55 c or nearly 2.2 inches of rubber. That’s the size of tires on some MTBs.
Yet, the real treat that gravel riders can look forward to is the ability to use a suspension fork on this frame, allowing us to keep up with trends and creating a bicycle that really can be the go-to choice for most riding settings. Forks with up to 40 mm of travel are on the menu for this one and dropper posts too.
One little component that I want to attract your attention to is the down tube. Okay, so the Tambora’s down tube is not little, and that’s precisely what I want to point out; there’s a reason for its size.
Photo: Polygon Bikes Aside from the shape of the tube, which just screams “I can take what you throw at me,” and also a bit aerodynamic, it’s also where Polygon now integrates the PolyPocket storage system. We can bring along a kit for flats, tools, gels, and other “stuff.”
Yet, Polygon did not sacrifice mounts on the new platform, and for those of use that use gravel bikes to ride to the edge of town and beyond, camping out under the stars in the process, be happy to know that we find mounts all over the frameset. The fork has them, the seat tube has them and the down tube too, but lacks mounts for fenders; this one’s dirty!
Personally, I’d love taking this beast out for a spin, and with complete bikes starting at $1,800, most of us are sure to be thinking the same thing. In time, you can add better components to it and still end up with a $4,500 ride after a year of pumping cash into it. Nice!

The cargo arm of Lufthansa Group said Monday it has agreed to purchase the Frankfurt operation of Fiege Air Cargo Logistics GmbH, bringing cargo handling operations at its Frankfurt hub under direct management, three weeks after completing the acquisition of another German cargo handling agent at the airport.
The transaction reflects Lufthansa Cargo’s ( XETRA: LHA ) recent strategy to become more vertically integrated in the air logistics sector. By reducing the number of shipment transfers to third-party vendors the company ostensibly can provide more reliable service and sell that as an advantage over other carriers that rely on airport services companies to move cargo between trucks and aircraft.
The airport logistics provider, which also has branches at the Cologne/Bonn, Germany, and Zurich airports, will continue to help Lufthansa Cargo recruiting, training and providing specialized warehouse personnel to handle air shipments, Lufthansa Cargo said. Fiege Air Cargo is part of logistics services conglomerate Fiege Logistik Stiftung & Co. KG. It took over the physical cargo handling for Lufthansa in Frankfurt in 2020.
Lufthansa Cargo is currently the No. 14 carrier in the world, by traffic volume, according to the International Air Transport Association . It operates 12 Boeing 777 freighter aircraft and is able to market capacity on six 777s operated by AeroLogic, a joint venture between Lufthansa and DHL Express, for a total of 18 widebody freighters under its control. It also manages the belly capacity of sister airlines Lufthansa Airlines, Austrian Airlines, Brussels Airlines, Discover Airlines and SunExpress to transport freight.
“We offer our customers high-quality and reliable solutions. Frankfurt is the most important hub in our network. In addition to significant investments in our new infrastructure and warehouse systems, a key question is how we can best operate this infrastructure. Taking full responsibility for handling operations is a logical step in this regard. This will allow us to introduce new technologies and automate our warehouse more quickly thanks to leaner structures, thereby enhancing quality and efficiency. In this way, we are setting the course for a successful future for the company. At the same time, we are pleased that we will continue our good cooperation with Fiege on a new basis over the long term,” said Frank Bauer, chief operations officer at Lufthansa Cargo, in a news release.
Terms of the deal, which still requires customary regulatory review, were not disclosed.
Why It Matters: The planned acquisition is part of Lufthansa Cargo’s strategic growth plan. The company’s goal is to return to the top three global air cargo providers by 2030. In addition to the consistent further development of its core business, Lufthansa Cargo is making targeted investments in measures to expand capacity, increase efficiency, and automate operations to support global businesses.
On Nov. 2, Lufthansa Cargo completed the acquisition of LUG air cargo handling GmbH from the Dettmer Group to increase warehouse capacity and operational flexibility in German, and exert more direct control of shipments during their journey versus using outside agents. LUG continues to operate as its own brand within Lufthansa Cargo and continues to support existing customers besides Lufthansa Cargo.
The additional ground handling capacity provided by LUG at Frankfurt International Airport complements Lufthansa Cargo’s existing infrastructure, including the $682 million cargo terminal expansion and modernization project scheduled for completion in 2030.
Lufthansa Cargo has since installed Uwe Glunz, a veteran company manager, and Patrik Tschirch, managing director of LUG, as co-CEOs of LUG.
The company earlier this year merged heyworld, which focuses on providing expedited cross-border shipping for e-commerce shipments and CB Customs Broker, into a new company called GlobeCross GmbH.
Q3 results
In the third quarter, Lufthansa Cargo tripled operating profit year over year to 162 million euros (equivalent to $177 million) behind a 28% increase in core transportation revenue as the airline picked up business from Middle East carriers heavily impacted by the Iran conflict. The reduction of industry capacity and the hike in jet fuel prices led to a 22% increase in yields. Demand was driven by continued strong business in the Asia/Pacific region in particular, as well as in the Americas.
Lufthansa’s cargo subsidiary achieved an adjusted operating margin of 15.6%, up from 6% in the comparable period.

Acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas called the approval of BridgeBio’s limb-girdle muscular dystrophy therapy “a historic milestone” for patients and families living with the disease.
There is now an FDA-approved, disease-modifying treatment for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy. The U.S. regulator gave the nod to BridgeBio’s Welgemda as the first medicine for this rare, genetic muscle disease.
In the FDA’s announcement on Monday afternoon, acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas called the approval “a historic milestone” for patients and families living with limb-girdle muscular dystrophy.
Welgemda, also known as BBP-418, is intended for adults and children with limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9 (LGMD2I/R9) who weigh at least 30 kg, or 66 lbs.
“Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy is a progressive muscle disease that gradually takes away a patient’s ability to walk, breathe, and live independently, often beginning in childhood,” Laura Jawidzik, director of the Division of Neurology 2 in the FDA’s Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER), said in a prepared statement. “The clinical data supporting Welgemda’s approval show meaningful improvements in walking speed and lung function, and we are encouraged by what that can mean for patients’ daily lives.”
There are over 30 subtypes of limb girdle muscular dystrophy, Christine Siu, CEO of BridgeBio’s neuromuscular division, told BioSpace earlier this month. Welgemda is the first targeted treatment for any form of the disease.
Rare diseases
BridgeBio gears up for rare muscular dystrophy launch with FDA approval in sight
If approved, BridgeBio Pharma’s BBP-418—which, according to one Jefferies analyst, boasts “pretty darn compelling” data—would be the first therapy for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy. The FDA has an action date of Nov. 27.
November 2, 2026
·
6 min read
·
Michael Gibney
Read more
LGMD2I/R9 is caused by mutations in the FKRP gene that lead to reduced levels of the encoded protein, impairing a cellular process called glycosylation and ultimately destabilizing and damaging muscles. BBP-418 is an oral glycosylation substrate therapy designed to increase FKRP, which in turn leads to higher levels of glycosylated alpha-dystroglycan (αDG), a common biomarker for the disease.
The approval was supported by results from the Phase 3 FORTIFY study , which enrolled 112 patients 12 to 60 years of age with LGMD2I/R9. FORTIFY met the primary interim analysis endpoint at 12 months, showing a statistically significant increase in glycosylated αDG in patients treated with the drug compared to “approximately no change” in the placebo group from baseline to three months, BridgeBio reported in October 2025. Welgemda also met the trial’s secondary endpoints, showing an increase in glycosylated αDG and a reduction in serum CK, a biomarker for muscle damage.
The FDA nod for Welgemda was largely expected, with Jefferies analyst Andrew Tsai giving the therapy higher than 90% odds of approval by the FDA’s deadline, which was November 27. In an interview earlier this month with BioSpace , Tsai based this prediction on the results of FORTIFY.
BridgeBio has identified more than 500 prospective patients in the U.S. while guiding toward potentially thousands more given adequate genetic testing and diagnosis. Based on this, Tsai predicted a market opportunity of greater than $1 billion annually at peak sales for Welgemda.
BridgeBio has been on a positive run of late. In June, the company reported that its oral achondroplasia drug infigratinib not only boosts growth in children but also significantly boosts body proportionality—a result Jefferies analysts at the time called “compelling.”

BridgeBio Pharma plans to file for approval in the third quarter. If granted, the oral drug could present a “highly differentiated” option over current achondroplasia therapies, according to Jefferies.

The FDA accepted the company’s new drug application for infigratinib in achondroplasia—the most common cause of dwarfism—in October and set a target action of February 4, 2027.
Three months earlier, in July, BridgeBio touted protective kidney benefits in Phase 2 and 3 trials of its transthyretin amyloidosis cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) drug Attruby, which Jefferies said is “distinct” from other medicines in this competitive space.

source_document.body:
Few topics in transportation draw more attention right now than artificial intelligence. Carriers want to know what it means for their workforce and their bottom line, and the loudest version of the debate asks whether AI will replace the people who run trucking operations.
Danielle Villegas, chief product and technology officer at PCS Software, Inc., has a different framing. In an appearance on FreightWaves’ What the Truck?!? , she described AI as a force multiplier: a tool that takes on repetitive work so people can spend their time on decisions that matter.
“It really just multiplies the efficiency of your team versus replacing anybody that you have,” Villegas said.
Automating the routine, freeing the dispatcher
For Villegas, the starting point is identifying the tasks dispatchers repeat every day. Routine notifications, such as on-time or delayed delivery updates, and load entry are prime candidates. Automating them gives dispatchers room to find more freight and handle exceptions, like a truck breaking down and a replacement driver having to be arranged.
That approach also changes what AI is for. Rather than treating it only as a way to cut costs, Villegas frames it as a way to expand what a dispatch team can do, from workforce capacity to revenue potential. Her description of the work AI should absorb is blunt: “letting AI do all of those boring, mundane things for you.”
Why the human stays accountable
The efficiency case comes with a caveat. Villegas said anyone who has spent time with AI tools knows their limits. “Sometimes AI is confidently wrong when it’s wrong,” she said.
That is why PCS builds its products around human oversight, particularly for consequential decisions. “You have to keep the human in the loop, especially when dollars or safety is concerned,” Villegas said.
Rates are the clearest example. If an AI system proposes the wrong one, the effect lands directly on the bottom line. “Margins are thin, especially for carriers,” she said. Her model is for AI to make recommendations and speed up decisions while a person makes the final call: “There’s a human pressing that button, saying, ‘Yep, that’s the right rate.’”
To explain why visibility matters, Villegas pointed to the camera inside a Waymo. The passenger display isn’t there because the vehicle needs it. It’s there to build confidence. “It gives you the confidence that the Waymo sees the person crossing the street,” she said. The same logic applies in freight, where users need to see what the AI is proposing and why.
Inside Cortex: 40-plus data elements
That transparency principle shapes how PCS designed driver assignment in Cortex. According to Villegas, the feature draws on more than 40 data elements to recommend which driver should haul which load. Those inputs include dispatcher knowledge, hours of service , stop times, how far a driver is willing to travel and whether the driver needs to get home.
Dispatcher history matters because, as Villegas put it, “there’s going to be knowledge inside of a dispatcher’s head that no technology, no LLM, no software in the world is ever going to have.”
The system then shows its work. Users can see the margin and the deadhead they would take on with a given driver. Cortex can also evaluate loads together rather than one at a time. “If you put three loads together, you’re going to reduce your deadhead,” Villegas said, noting that a load-by-load view might miss the combination entirely.
An assist, not a hostile takeover
Villegas said the line for AI autonomy comes down to explainability. If a system can’t show where its recommendation came from, users should question it. She added that the stakes are higher because AI isn’t only available to legitimate operators.
“It cannot be a black box because not only the good guys are using AI, the bad guys are using it as well,” she said.
Her prescription is visibility plus control. “You have to have that visibility, and you have to be able to turn it off,” Villegas said. She was equally direct about the role AI should play: “It’s an assist and not a hostile takeover. If it’s a hostile takeover, you can’t have that accountability.”
Meeting customers where they are
Through PCS’s early adopter program, Villegas said, the company has learned that customers vary widely in how much automation they want. Some welcome AI that builds a load from a PDF, work that spares dispatchers from keying it in by hand. Others want AI to reach out on its own, without a person clicking a button.
PCS’s answer is a configurable, rules-based approach that determines when AI assists and when it acts. “Each customer is different,” Villegas said, and the pace varies: “Some of them want to crawl before they run, and some of them want to run.”
Customer attitudes have shifted as well. When PCS first introduced Cora, its voice AI agent, interest was low. “Nope, AI voice agents. I don’t want to talk to them,” Villegas said, recalling the early reaction. Today, she said, the request is different. “I want more Cora,” customers tell her. In her words, “It’s a choose-your-own-adventure.”
Finding backhauls without losing control
One of Cora’s uses is backhaul outreach. Villegas said PCS’s market research found customers losing hundreds of thousands of dollars because they lacked the dispatch staff to find return loads, leaving trucks to run empty to the next pickup. The system identifies opportunities, including through load board connections, and Cora can make high-volume calls to freight sources far faster than a dispatcher placing one call at a time.
Even here, a person stays in charge. Cora assembles opportunities for review rather than dispatching anything on its own. “It’s not a load that automatically comes in that says, ‘Hey, this is getting dispatched,’” Villegas said. “You get to check the rate. You get to make sure all the details make sense before you’re putting a driver onto that backhaul.”
Practicing what PCS preaches
PCS applies the same principle inside its own walls. Villegas said the company rolled out Claude internally and let AI handle tasks like drafting software tickets and tracking customer issues and planned enhancements, with people reviewing the results and the testing. She described the path to getting value as hands-on. “I think it’s just a lot of trial and error, to be completely honest, and leaning into it,” she said.
The message to customers is the same one PCS follows itself: “Let your people manage the exceptions and let the AI manage those routine tasks.”
The question to ask every AI vendor
With new AI vendors appearing constantly, Villegas was asked what question a trucking company should put to one before signing. Her answer centered on proof. “What are the results it’s going to give me, and how do I know that it’s working?” she said, adding, “Show me why you got that result.”
She said buyers should also ask which of their own data a vendor’s system relies on. “AI is only as smart as the data it has access to,” Villegas said.
Where the human-AI relationship goes next
Looking ahead, Villegas expects progress to come through trust, not sudden disruption. “I think it’s really kind of building the trust with it,” she said. “I think it’s going to be a little slow at first.”
As users get comfortable, she expects the way they work with transportation management software to change. “It kind of becomes more of a headless application more than anything else,” Villegas said, adding that shippers and carriers will demand more from their software vendors. The change isn’t limited to developers, either. “I’ve got truckers that are vibe coding out there right now,” she said.
That momentum raises the importance of guardrails. “You don’t want AI to run rampant,” Villegas said. For any vendor, she said, the safeguards come back to the same few principles: “You have to be able to turn it off. You have to have that human in the loop.”
Her closing point returned to accountability. “Someone has to be able to control it,” Villegas said.

BYD Ti7 (top) and Land Rover Defender 110 (bottom) in side profile (Source: BYD UK, JLR)
A Dutch court has barred BYD from selling or building its Ti7 SUV anywhere in the European Union after ruling that it infringes Jaguar Land Rover’s registered design for the Land Rover Defender. Breaking the injunction costs BYD €100,000 per day, up to €10 million.
It’s a sharp turnaround from 10 days ago, when the same court in The Hague handed BYD an early win in the Defender copycat fight . BYD’s Hong Kong shares fell as much as 4% on Monday before closing 1.9% lower.
The court says the Ti7 looks like a Defender
The preliminary relief judge at the District Court of The Hague issued the ruling on Friday, November 20, in summary proceedings JLR brought against 11 BYD companies .
JLR put six registered EU designs in front of the court. The judge only needed one of them: design 005248580-0004, registered in April 2018 and covering the current Defender 110, known internally as the L663.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
According to the ruling, the elements that dominate that design are the rounded “shoulders,” the rounded corners, the signature panel on the C-pillar, the rounded wheel-arch cutouts, the continuous window line, and the overall silhouette. The court found every one of them on the Ti7.
Here’s how the two SUVs compare from the same angles, using official press images from BYD and JLR:
Side profile, front three-quarter and front views: BYD Ti7 (left) vs Land Rover Defender 110 (right) (Source: BYD UK, JLR)
BYD argued that the headlights, grille, bumpers, hood and side profile are all different. Not enough, said the judge, who ruled that those differences, on their own or combined, don’t give an informed user a different overall impression. The court also found the Ti7 sits closer to the Defender than to older boxy SUVs like the Ford Flex, Jeep Wrangler and Mercedes G-Class.
Banned from a market it hasn’t entered yet
BYD doesn’t sell the Ti7 in the EU. It told the court it has “no concrete plans” to launch it there and that the SUV can only be ordered in the UK.
The judge didn’t buy that as a defense. By BYD’s own account, it developed the seven-seat layout for the UK and Europe, a promotional video called the Ti7 the first seven-seat SUV “in Europe,” and BYD wouldn’t commit to keeping it out of the EU. That was enough for the court to find a threat of infringement.
So BYD’s EU entities can no longer import, produce, offer, sell, store or supply the Ti7. The order kicks in one week after the ruling is formally served, and it even covers BYD’s Hungarian unit, since the judge considered it conceivable the Ti7 could come out of the new Szeged factory.
The UK is a different story. The court said it has no jurisdiction over BYD UK and threw out JLR’s UK design claims, so British deliveries are still on for January 2027. That’s the one European market where BYD actually opened orders, pricing the Ti7 at £47,995 , about £24,000 below the £71,840 plug-in Defender 110.
BYD said it “strongly disagrees” with the judgment and will appeal, adding that the Ti7 “is the result of BYD’s own independent design work and infringes none of JLR’s rights.” JLR told AFP it protects its intellectual property and takes legal action when necessary.
What happens next
BYD has four weeks to appeal, but the injunction stays in force while it does. JLR, for its part, has six months to file a full case on the merits, or BYD can get the injunction lifted.
There’s more coming. JLR also has a separate case in Rotterdam over copyright and “slavish imitation,” with a hearing scheduled for Wednesday.
This whole thing started in August, when JLR had bailiffs raid BYD’s Dutch offices in Schiedam and Hoofddorp. The court later ordered JLR to destroy everything it seized, saying it didn’t need BYD’s internal files to make its design case. And it didn’t. JLR won on the design registration alone.
Electrek’s Take
The Ti7 looks like a Defender. We said so when BYD first brought it to the UK , and so did pretty much everyone else. Chinese automakers have been building Defender lookalikes for years, but most of them stayed in China.
BYD brought one to the Defender’s home turf at a £24,000 discount, so a fight with JLR was always coming.
Top comment by *Rich
Liked by 3 people
As a consumer, I would consider one element extremely different between the two vehicles -- build quality. Land Rover has a reputation in that department. So does BYD. I would buy the BYD on that alone in the BBB (big,boxy,brick) "category" of vehicle. Is that what JLR is really worried about?
View all comments
But honestly, all these boxy SUVs look the same to me.
Nobody owns “boxy.” JLR even failed to trademark the classic Defender’s shape in the UK, a fight it lost in its legal battle with the Ineos Grenadier. But it registered the new Defender’s design in 2018, and that specific combination of shoulders, C-pillar panel and wheel arches is exactly what the court protected. That’s how design rights are supposed to work.
The actual business damage is small for now. The Ti7 sells roughly 30,000 units a month, almost all in China, and the UK launch goes ahead. The stock dip was about headlines more than lost Ti7 sales.

Toyota is overhauling its best-selling vehicle of all time, which will include the first fully electric Corolla.
When is Toyota launching the Corolla EV?
The Toyota Corolla is one of the most recognized and best-selling automotive nameplates of all time.
Since its debut in 1966, over 57 million drivers have chosen the Corolla thanks to its reliability, low cost of ownership, efficiency, and affordable price tag.
Toyota sells the Corolla in more than 150 countries and has expanded the lineup over the past 50 years from sedans and hatchbacks to coupes, wagons, a sporty GR Corolla, and the Corolla Cross compact SUV.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
For its 13th generation, Toyota is planning a major overhaul that’s expected to be its biggest transformation yet.
The next-gen Toyota Corolla will be based on a new “multipathway” platform that will support gas, hybrid, plug-in hybrid, and, for the first time, fully electric powertrains.
“Whether it’s a battery EV, plug-in hybrid, hybrid, or internal combustion engine vehicle ― whatever the power source ― let’s make good-looking cars that everyone will want to drive!” Toyota’s former president and current CEO Koji Sato said after unveiling the Corolla Concept at the Japan Mobility Show last October.
Toyota CEO Koji Sato reveals the Corolla Concept at the Japan Mobility Show (Source: Toyota)
Toyota has kept most details a secret, including battery and powertrain specs. However, the new version is expected to adopt a similar design to the concept.
“When we created the concept, we wanted to give the Corolla name a new twist,” Norihiko Kobayashi, who has led the Corolla program since 2011, told Motor.es during a recent interview.
The Corolla has undergone several minor updates over the past 60 years, but the next-gen model will look nothing like its predecessors.
Toyota Corolla Concept (Source: Toyota)
“It wasn’t simply about following in the footsteps of the past,” Kobayashi explained, “we wanted to delve into the future while still maintaining the Corolla identity.”
Developing the next-gen Corolla “wasn’t just about making a new car, but about redefining the future without looking back,” he added.
Like the current version, the new Toyota Corolla will come in several different body types, including a sedan, hatchback, crossover, and a GR variant.
Toyota CEO Koji Sato reveals the Corolla Concept at the Japan Mobility Show (Source: Toyota)
Details have yet to be confirmed, but the Toyota Corolla EV is expected to be available in single- and dual-motor configurations and offer a pure electric driving range of at least 250 miles.
The hybrid will reportedly use a new 1.5-liter four-cylinder engine and an electric motor. Toyota’s engineers told Car and Driver the hybrid system would deliver around 134 horsepower. It’s also estimated to be 10% to 20% more efficient than the current Corolla.
Toyota’s next-gen Corolla is expected to debut sometime in 2027 as a 2028 model year. According to Car and Driver , the gas version will likely start at around $25,000, the hybrid around $27,000, and the EV and PHEVs will likely be priced in the $30,000 range.

Posted By: Blair McBride November 23, 2026
Speculative investors reduced their net bullish positions in copper futures by nearly 39% in the latest reporting week, according to BMO Capital Markets, as selling pressure intensified amid uncertainty over U.S. tariffs and weakening enthusiasm for artificial intelligence investments. It was the eighth straight weekly decline.
Net bullish positions held by non-commercial traders in U.S. copper futures fell to 17,777 contracts as of Nov. 17, down from 28,904 a week earlier and at their lowest level since March 2025, BMO analysts Helen Amos and George Heppel said Monday, citing Commodity Futures Trading Commission data released Friday.
“Our conversations here in China over Asia Copper Week indicate onshore expectations are for the U.S. to abandon tariff policy, a view further fuelled by reports that tens of [thousands of tonnes] of cathode in the U.S. have been booked for direct dispatch to China,” Amos and Heppel said Friday in a note from Shanghai.
Yangshan premium down
China’s Yangshan warrant premium, a measure of demand for imported copper, eased to $450 (C$646) per tonne Monday from a record $500 last week, Reuters reported. Another 11,225 tonnes of copper were earmarked for removal from London Metal Exchange warehouses in Asia on Friday, with a trader and warehouse manager telling Reuters the metal was destined for China.
The sell-off has intensified as investors close positions betting on higher copper prices and increase wagers on further declines, BMO said Friday. The analysts said the exercise of put options, which give holders the right to sell at a predetermined price, has amplified the correction. Speculators shed 7,268 long contracts and added 3,859 short contracts over the week, the commission’s figures show.
Three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange traded at $12,193.50 per tonne as of 6:11 a.m. Toronto time Monday, up 0.3%, after briefly falling to $11,948, its lowest level since March 24, Reuters reported. Copper has lost almost 14% this month as investors question whether heavy spending on artificial intelligence will generate sufficient returns, despite tight physical supplies in China.
Copper reverses course
The analysts’ assessment came Friday as traders prepared to ship an estimated 30,000 to 100,000 tonnes of refined copper from the U.S. West Coast to China, a move BMO had previously considered highly unlikely. The shipments reverse a flow of metal into American warehouses ahead of possible U.S. import tariffs.
Meanwhile, Chilean producer Codelco, one of the world’s top copper producers, has offered Asian buyers annual contract premiums of $250 to $280 per tonne for 2027, compared with $350 for Chinese buyers this year, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the discussions. China imported just over 140,000 tonnes of Chilean cathode in the first nine months of 2026, down 38% from a year earlier.
Price outlook
BMO warned that downward pressure on copper prices could persist until the administration of President Donald Trump signals its tariff intentions or scrap and solvent extraction-electrowinning producers respond to market conditions.
A July 2025 White House proclamation imposed a 50% tariff on certain semi-finished copper products and derivatives, while leaving refined copper exempt pending further review. The administration is considering duties of 15% on refined copper from Jan. 1, 2027, and 30% from Jan. 1, 2028.
A signal from Washington could stop the slide. Otherwise, the red metal might have to fall far enough to curb scrap supply or higher-cost production from leaching, potentially to around $10,000 to $11,000 per tonne, Amos and Heppel said. BMO’s medium-term bullish view on copper is unchanged.
